text: {"findings":[{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"No experiment plan; full rollout","detail":"The proposal explicitly has no experiment plan and launches to all markets with only dashboard monitoring. There is no randomization, control group, duration, MDE, or power, so the incentive's effect cannot be measured.","evidence_quote":"None. We will roll out to all markets and monitor the dashboard.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Run a randomized test (e.g., zone- or time-block-level with spillover controls) for at least 14 days, with a defined MDE and power analysis, before any broad rollout."},{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Driver pay change without review","detail":"A surge incentive changes driver compensation, which is a pay-controlled area. The Reviews section says 'None', so no pay or policy review is recorded.","evidence_quote":"## Reviews And Dependencies\nNone.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Obtain and record the required pay/compensation policy review (and legal/finance sign-off as applicable) before launch."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing cost, service, and quality guardrails","detail":"A pay incentive needs guardrails like incentive cost per delivery/unit economics, delivery time or late rate, order cancellation/unassigned order rate, and driver retention/earnings. Only a neighboring-zone acceptance rate guardrail is given, and it has no threshold.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate in neighboring zones: should not drop.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails for incentive spend per order, on-time delivery rate, unassigned/cancelled order rate, and driver supply/retention, each with numeric thresholds."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Success metric misaligned and guardrail vague","detail":"The stated problem is unassigned orders due to short supply, yet the success metric is Driver Acceptance Rate, which does not measure that outcome. The guardrail 'should not drop' has no defined threshold, and the plan does not specify the evening-peak scope of the metric.","evidence_quote":"Driver Acceptance Rate: baseline 71%, target 78% within 4 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Use canonical glossary metrics tied to the problem (e.g., unassigned order rate, evening driver supply hours) and define the acceptance rate scope and guardrail thresholds."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Baseline and target lack source","detail":"The 71% baseline and 78% target are stated as fact without a data source, time window, or rationale for the expected 7-point lift.","evidence_quote":"baseline 71%, target 78% within 4 weeks","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the data source and period for the baseline, and justify the target using prior incentive results or a power analysis."}]}
